description: Octal 16-bit DAC SPI, internal reference
notes: GRADE LOCKED TO C. The grade letter selects REFERENCE GAIN as well as reset state - A/B are gain 1 (2.500V full scale), C/D are gain 2 (5.000V). An A-grade part would halve everything: pitch -2…+2.25V, mods +-5V, and channel 7 could not reach 2.500V at all. This row previously read 'DAC8568C (or A grade)' and explained the letter as reset state only. C also clears to ZERO scale where B/D clear to midscale and would park pitch octaves up. Populate 6 of 8: pitch, 4 mods, mod offset; channels 6 and 8 spare. Internal ref DISABLED by default, enable at boot. GAIN/GRADE MAPPING CONFIRMED 2026-09-21 against SBAS430E, now in the repo at datasheets/analog/DAC8568CIPW.pdf and verified verbatim: 'For device grades A and C on power-up, all DAC registers are filled with zeros and the output voltages of all DAC channels are set to zero scale.' A/B = 2.5V FSR, C/D = 5V FSR. *** TWO RIDERS THE REPO DID NOT HAVE. *** (1) THE C GRADE REQUIRES AVDD 5.0V TO 5.5V - the Electrical Characteristics table specifies grades C/D only over that range, where A/B are specified 2.7-5.5V. The LM317 nominal is 5.21V so this passes, but E7 SELECTS R-REG-SET ON THE BENCH over a 0.66V worst-case spread: a selection that lands below 5.00V puts the DAC out of spec. 5.00V is now a HARD FLOOR on that bench step, which it was not before. (2) EXTERNAL VREFIN MUST BE <= AVDD/2 ON C/D, against <= AVDD on A/B. Not binding today because the internal reference is used, but it forecloses an external-reference retrofit at anything above ~2.6V. Also from SBAS430E: reference tempco is GRADE-DEPENDENT - C/D are 2 typ / 5 max ppm/degC where A/B are 5 typ / 25 max, so the 5 ppm/degC in the pitch error budget is the C-grade MAX and is the right number. Static reference mode auto-powers the reference with the DACs; Flexible mode (DB19=1) keeps it up regardless, and BOTH default to reference OFF after any power cycle

CONFIRMED by the same document: the -1 option is the four-equal-10k 1:1 quad and there is no 1:3 option (full table p.2: -1 10k 1:1, -2 100k 1:1, -3 1:10, -4 1k 1:1, -5 1M 1:1, -6 1:5); grade A 0.01% / B 0.025%; ratio tracking 1 ppm/degC MAX (0.2 typ), so the 0.027 cents/10degC pitch-budget line is conservatively sourced; all three order codes appear verbatim in the p.3 table. description: Instrumentation amp - breath receiver, senses against AGND
notes: BREATH drives IN-, AGND drives IN+, REF is driven by TRIM-BREATH-ZERO through a BUFFER - never a bare divider, since source impedance on an in-amp REF pin degrades CMRR one-for-one. *** THE NUMBER IS 5 OHMS: *** SBOS792A, now in the repo at datasheets/analog/INA828IDR.pdf, section 8.1 verbatim - 'For the best performance, keep the source impedance to the REF terminal, RREF, below 5 ohm' - because RREF sits in series with one of the internal 40k difference-amp resistors and unbalances the bridge. The buffer was already right; it now has a spec to be right against. Output is 0V at rest to -9.6V at full (Vout = -2.185*(V_BREATH - V_AGND) + V_REF, with TRIM-BREATH-ZERO nulling the sensor pedestal). This field read "-0.44V at rest to -10V at full" until 2026-09-21 - that is the UN-NULLED output from before REF carried a trimmer, and trimming to it at E10 leaves the downstream stage ~1.8V off zero at the working gain; the downstream stage inverts, which is also the topology that does gain-then-offset with two pots in one op-amp half. The DAC ch6 zero injection that originally justified the input swap is deleted (ADR 0003). EMI: the part HAS an integrated RFI filter, -3dB at 53MHz, and EMIRR is a TABULATED characteristic not just a curve. WORST CASES ARE 48dB DIFFERENTIAL AT 400MHz AND 51dB COMMON-MODE AT 1.8GHz - note the differential and common-mode columns INVERT between 900MHz (52/98) and 1.8GHz (94/51), so any RF-rectification argument must use those two and not the 90-plus dB numbers. TI does not claim the internal filter is sufficient on its own. See hardware/module/breath-receive-stage/breath-receive-stage.md

That is what makes back-driving an unpowered module safe. V_IH 2.0V min and V_IL 0.8V max CONFIRMED - TTL levels, not ratioed to VCC - which is the threshold the R-SPI-SER analysis is built on. What it was protecting against - floating CMOS at the DAC while the instrument is off - is what R-SPI-PULL's six resistors are for, and running the buffer unconditionally is what every surveyed Eurorack module does

With RthJL 15C/W, RthJA 50C/W and ~0.45W at 1.0A, a 65C ambient puts the lead near 81C - inside the knee, with roughly 9C of ambient headroom. BUT RthJA 50C/W is specified for the datasheet's own mounting: vertical PCB, 9.5mm leads, 38x38mm copper pads. A worse mount invalidates the margin. SS34 (Vishay 88751, 3A SMA) and 1N5822 (3A DO-27) are banked as alternatives if E6 measures hot THREE not two: the module's analog +12V and the umbilical feed must NOT share a diode - instrument current then modulates its Vf by ~80mV, which is ~20 cents of breath-correlated pitch bend and needs no ground path at all (ADR 0006) | 2026-09-21: the '20 cents of breath-correlated pitch bend' this row used to cite as the reason for the THIRD diode is refuted - the real figure is five orders of magnitude smaller, because pitch references the DAC's INTERNAL reference and not this rail. The value and its whole derivation are the tracked figure diode-split-rationale, owned by hardware/module/power-entry/power-entry.md, and are deliberately NOT restated here | 2026-09-21: THIS ROW CARRIED 0.00029 cents, AND THAT WAS ALREADY THE THIRD OF FOUR DIFFERENT LIVE VALUES for one quantity - 0.00018 in ADR 0004, 0.00027 in ADR 0006, 0.00029 here, 0.00044 in the register. A bleeder sized for TI's 2.5mA UNDER-LOADS a 3.5mA part. Either name the manufacturer or size for the worst case across candidates. Verified by rendering the sheet and reading it by hand - the file is vector CAD. Specs off the drawing: Z@100MHz 600 nominal / 450 min / 750 max, DCR 0.080 ohm max, rated 1500 mA, 3.20 x 1.60 x 1.10 mm, -40 to +125degC including self-heating. *** THE '>=1A' RULE DOES NOT DO WHAT THIS ROW SAYS IT DOES. *** The row's reason is 'a saturated bead is a wire' - but a bead's CURRENT RATING IS THERMAL, NOT MAGNETIC, so it tells you nothing about saturation. Read off this part's own bias curve at 100 MHz: 0 A ~614 ohm, 250 mA ~431, 500 mA ~157, 1000 mA ~72, 1500 mA (its RATED current) ~51. To prove the point a 3000 mA part in the same package with the same 600 ohm nominal was banked alongside it (HI1206N601R-10-ferrite-bead.pdf): at 500 mA it reads ~145 ohm, i.e. SLIGHTLY WORSE than the 1.5 A part. Doubling the rating buys nothing but 0.02 ohm of DCR. *** WHAT THIS MEANS PER BRANCH: *** FB4 (+5V, mA), FB3 (-12V, 10-20mA) and FB1 (+12V analog, ~45mA) all sit on the flat part of the curve and get 580-614 ohm, essentially the nameplate. No 1206 600R bead of any rating fixes FB2; the bias curve shifts the impedance peak UP IN FREQUENCY, so the bead does not die, its useful band simply slides off 100 MHz. EITHER the requirement for FB2 is restated at its real operating current, or FB2 becomes a physically larger part. IR DROP at 0.080 ohm max: 28.7 mV at 359 mA (10.3 mW), 31.4 mV at 392 mA, 3.6 mV at 45 mA. SECOND SOURCE: Murata BLM31PG601SN1L is an electrical twin and far better stocked, but MURATA'S PDF CARRIES NO DC-BIAS CURVE EITHER - that data lives only in SimSurfing - so it can be an alternate flagged 'bias assumed, not documented', never the characterised part. description: Fault timer capacitor for U-LOADSW
notes: BLOCKING. 10nF was wrong by 12x to 300x and gave a 0.16-4ms fault timer, so the module latched off at the end of every start. Three reviewers found this independently. C = I_TIMER x t / 1.233V; target t = 150ms, which is 2.4x the ~62ms current-limited start that foldback forces. That is 365nF if I_TIMER is 3uA and 9.25uF if it is 76uA - the reviewers disagree and the datasheet decides. READ THE LT1641 DATASHEET BEFORE ORDERING. The old 0805 C0G package is wrong for any value in that range | 2026-09-21: the dispute RESOLVES to the 76uA camp, and both reviewers were half right - TIMER is pulled DOWN at 3uA whenever the current-limit amp is idle, and an 80uA pull-up is switched in while it is ACTIVE, so the ramp runs at a net ~77uA. C = 77uA x 150ms / 1.233V = 9.4uF, PROVISIONAL. Still BLOCKING, on provenance not on ignorance: that is search-index datasheet text, not a verified PDF (analog.com unreachable through four waves; see datasheets/MANIFEST.csv). At ~9uF this is electrolytic or large ceramic, where LEAKAGE IS A MEANINGFUL FRACTION OF THE 3uA PULL-DOWN - specify a low-leakage part or the timer never resets | 2026-09-21 VALUE SET, NO LONGER BLOCKING. 164112fc.pdf is banked at datasheets/discrete-and-power/LT1641.pdf. The 77uA net ramp is CONFIRMED VERBATIM [p.8]: 'When the current limit circuitry is not active, the TIMER pin is pulled to GND by a 3uA current source. After the current limit circuit becomes active, an 80uA pull-up current source is connected to the TIMER pin and the voltage will rise with a slope equal to 77uA/CTIMER.' Both reviewers were half right exactly as this row already said. ADI's own shorthand C(nF) = 62 x t(ms) [p.8] gives 9.30uF for 150ms against the 9.37uF the exact form gives. SET TO 10uF, not 9.4uF, for two reasons: 9.4uF is not a stock value, and the pull-up's newly-read bounds (-24/-80/-132uA, p.2) make the fault time 587/160/95.6 ms at 10uF - and 95.6ms against the 47.5ms worst-case hot-plug start is 2.01x, where 9.4uF gives 1.89x. THE 150ms TARGET WAS NEVER THE SPEC; exceeding the current-limited start on worst-case silicon is. Datasheet hard minimum is 1.5nF [p.5], not binding here. The 0805 C0G package this row used to carry is wrong by three orders of magnitude, hence the package change. LEAKAGE: at 10uF this is electrolytic or large ceramic and leakage is a meaningful fraction of the 3uA pull-down - specify a low-leakage part or the timer never resets

description: Gate capacitor programming the load switch ramp
notes: BLOCKING, AND IT DID NOT EXIST. There was no gate capacitor in the BOM or the schematic, yet the FET sizing, the boot analysis and ADR 0005's 50-100ms ramp specification all rest on a 'programmed ramp'. With the FET's bare Ciss (~1nF) and ~10uA of gate current the ramp is 10kV/s, which demands 2.2mF x 10kV/s = 22A - twenty-odd times the limit. C = I_GATE / (dV/dt); a 100ms ramp is 120V/s, so ~83nF | 2026-09-21: I_GATE is 10uA TYPICAL with NO MIN/MAX established, so 83nF is a ramp spec with an unbounded tolerance. Still BLOCKING on the PDF at 10uA. READ I_GATE OFF THE LT1641 DATASHEET BEFORE ORDERING | 2026-09-21 VALUE SET, NO LONGER BLOCKING. I_GATE IS 10uA TYPICAL AND IT DOES HAVE MIN/MAX: I_GATEUP = -5 / -10 / -20 uA [164112fc p.2], corroborated independently by the DC1354A demo quick-start guide p.1. That answers this row's open question and it answers it badly: a 4:1 window. SET TO 82nF (E24; 83nF is not orderable), which gives dV/dt = 61 / 122 / 244 V/s and a ramp to 12V of 197 / 98 / 49 ms. *** ADR 0005's '50-100ms ramp' IS NOT ACHIEVABLE WITH THIS PART *** - no single capacitor can hold a 4:1 current spread inside a 2:1 time window. 82nF centres the TYPICAL at 98ms, inside ADR 0005; the guaranteed envelope is 49-197ms. Raised against ADR 0005; ADR 0005 must widen the spec or the ramp must be programmed by something other than the internal pull-up. Both corners are safe: 537mA of charging at the fast corner still clears the 240mA foldback floor at 0.14V of output and never approaches 940mA
